long_biography.plain_text:
Naftasib established Mikhail Khimich's commercial standing long before his New Zealand investments. He served as general director through the 1990s, became a half-owner and remained deputy general director as the Russian company bought, processed and supplied oil products. That combination of operating control and equity defined the business record on which his later investments rested.

In Auckland, Khimich pursued a different kind of expansion. After encountering Waiwera artesian water, he acquired a majority stake in the bottling company and thermal resort, later taking full control. He worked on premium branding, spirits and export plans while running the group between Russia and New Zealand. Government approvals tied further land investment to a bottling plant and later an organic winery, but the projects stalled. Waiwera's companies entered liquidation, and Khimich was declared bankrupt before his death in Moscow.

Khimich disclosed day-to-day Naftasib leadership beginning in 1991, later 50 per cent ownership and continued executive service, and reporting describes him as having made his fortune in oil and other business activity. That supports broad Self-made. Public sources do not reveal how he acquired the Naftasib stake or whether family capital, a buyout or another starting platform was involved, so no narrower subtype is asserted.

No sufficiently reliable public source was found for Khimich's date or place of birth or a patronymic or middle name. Name-only search results for other Mikhail Khimich identities were rejected, and no birth detail is proposed.

No dedicated Forbes profile or identity-verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or Personal Website was found. Defunct or organisational Waiwera pages do not qualify as current exact-person profiles, so no social is proposed.

Contemporary sources variously date Khimich's initial involvement to 2009 or 2010, reflecting the difference between commercial acquisition activity and regulatory approval. The biographies avoid assigning a disputed year and preserve the documented sequence from majority stake to full ownership.

The direct SuperyachtNews interview uses Thalia only to bridge the frozen relationship to the exact Waiwera owner. Neither biography, classification, proposed detail nor tag depends on the vessel, its specifications or its sale history.

Oil & gas is the minimum useful active tag supported by Khimich's long Naftasib operating and ownership record. Waiwera's beverage and hospitality operations are preserved in the biographies, but they did not become the durable source of his wealth and do not justify an additional active tag.
